text:
Seattle needed two goals in the last six minutes to settle a game it never really controlled. Mackie Samoskevich put the Kraken ahead 4-3 at 14:35 of the third, and Frederick Gaudreau sealed the 5-3 win with an unassisted goal at 19:00, on what the data rates as a 60% chance. That one came with the visitors pressing, and the two goals took a game that had been tied since Logan Cooley's second of the night at 7:42.

The way it was played tells a different story from the score. Utah had 71 shot attempts to Seattle's 51 and 36 shots on goal to 23. Seattle's win probability, built from simulated replays of every shot, comes out at 37% for the Kraken and 63% for Utah. At even strength the gap was wide: Utah's chances were worth 1.88 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) against 0.7 for Seattle. Seattle did the damage elsewhere. Jordan Eberle opened the scoring on a slap shot the data gave a 1% chance, and Matty Beniers and Brandon Montour scored on power plays. Utah's Karel Vejmelka allowed 2.1 more goals than the quality of his 22 shots against would suggest, while Philipp Grubauer stopped 33 of 36 and was named second star.

Cooley's two goals, both set up by Mikhail Sergachev, had pulled Utah level after it trailed 3-1 early in the second, but the late finishing went Seattle's way. Samoskevich was first star and Eberle, with a goal and an assist, was third. The facts here don't include streaks or standings for either club, so the result stands as one game: a win Seattle took with its chances, and a loss Utah took despite most of the play.
